0.long_answer: Hodgkin's lymphoma accounts for roughly 10% of all lymphoma cases. It is well established that about half of Hodgkin's lymphoma cases are associated with Epstein–Barr virus (EBV) infection. EBV can be detected in the malignant Reed‐Sternberg cells in EBV-positive cases and is thought to contribute to the pathogenesis of the disease. This association, while not present in all cases, underlines the role that viral infections can play in the development of certain lymphomas.
